observations: Photo 0 shows the back panel of a desktop tower with multiple ports, including USB, Ethernet, and video outputs, and a large vented area. The case is wrapped in plastic.

Photo 1 and Photo 2 show the same tower wrapped in plastic with a handwritten note taped to it. The note reads: 'DELL PRECISION 7920 TOWER SILVER 4110 CPU 16CORES 32GB - RAM 800GB - SSD RTX GEFORCE 3080 10GB WINDOWS 11 PRO.'
The tower appears to be a Dell Precision workstation, based on the note and the design of the back panel.
The note is handwritten and not an official label; it is taped to the plastic wrap.
The model 'Precision 7920' is visible on the note, but not on the chassis itself in any photo.
No visible branding or model number on the chassis in photo 0 or 2; only the note provides the model.
The note claims an RTX 3080 10GB GPU, which is a consumer-grade card, while the Dell Precision 7920 is typically equipped with professional-grade Quadro GPUs. This is a red flag.
The note also claims Windows 11 Pro, which is not visible in any photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 and Photo 2 show a handwritten note stating 'DELL PRECISION 7920 TOWER'.
The note in photo 1 and 2 states 'SILVER 4110 CPU 16CORES', but there is no visible CPU or label to confirm this. The model number is not readable on the chassis.
The note in photo 1 and 2 states '32GB - RAM', but there is no visible RAM module or label to confirm this. The internal components are not shown.
The note in photo 1 and 2 states '800GB - SSD', but there is no visible storage drive or label to confirm this. The internal components are not shown.

The note in photo 1 and 2 states 'RTX GEFORCE 3080 10GB', but the Dell Precision 7920 is a professional workstation and typically uses Quadro GPUs, not consumer GeForce cards. This is inconsistent with the product line. No GPU is visible in any photo.
The note in photo 1 and 2 states 'WINDOWS 11 PRO', but there is no screen or boot-up image to verify the OS. This cannot be confirmed remotely.

risks.proof: A photo of the internal GPU with its label visible, or a screenshot of the device manager showing the GPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it has a consumer-grade GPU, which is less valuable for professional workloads.

risks.risk: The OS is claimed to be Windows 11 Pro, but there is no proof of installation or license. It may be unlicensed or not installed at all.
